translation.literal: “Tat savituḥ”: to the Brahmā-self, to the heart, namaḥ. “Vareṇyam”: to the Viṣṇu-self, to the head, svāhā. “Bhargo devasya”: to the Rudra-self, to the tuft, vaṣaṭ. “Dhīmahi”: to the Īśvara-self, to the armour, hum. “Dhiyo yo naḥ”: to the Sadāśiva-self, to the three eyes, vauṣaṭ. “Pracodayāt”: to the Self of all, to the weapon, phaṭ. “Bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar om” — thus the binding of the directions.
translation.readable: The six parts of the Gāyatrī, each with its deity, are placed on the body: heart, head, tuft, the ‘armour’ of the crossed arms, the three eyes, and the ‘weapon’, each with its own ritual call (namaḥ, svāhā, vaṣaṭ, hum, vauṣaṭ, phaṭ); then bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar om binds the directions.

sandhi_exceptions.note: the nyāsa formula is said in parts — the word of the Gāyatrī, the deity, the place — with a pause between them; the witness leaves the vowels unjoined

meaning: The second nyāsa: the same six parts of the Gāyatrī and the same six deities as the kara-nyāsa, now placed on the body — the heart, the head, the tuft of hair, the ‘armour’, the three eyes and the ‘weapon’ — each closed with its own ritual call. The last line, with the three vyāhṛtis and om, ‘binds the directions’ around the worshipper for the japa; it is undone after the japa (dig-vimoka).
in_the_rite: Step nyāsa, all three services, after the kara-nyāsa, in the Mylapore prayoga only.

notes.label: traditional
notes.text: The places and calls (hṛdaya namaḥ, śiras svāhā, śikhā vaṣaṭ, kavaca hum, netra vauṣaṭ, astra phaṭ) are the six members of the common aṅga-nyāsa; M gives them for the Gāyatrī. S has no nyāsa.

flags.text: As for kara-nyāsa: M writes तत्स॑वि॒तुः ब्रह्मात्मने unjoined (proposed तत्स॑वि॒तुर्ब्रह्मात्मने), and the svara marks in the text must be stripped before the word-division proof. With both, the padaccheda rejoins (declared pauses: धीमहि·ईश्वरात्मने, सर्वात्मने·अस्त्राय).
